rv.q: Peter Friedman and Sydney Lemmon are awesome in playwright Max Wolf Friedlich's galvanizing psychological thriller.
Max Wolf Friedlich's 'Job' is as tense as a thriller, as compelling as a psychological drama and as up-to-date as tomorrow's headlines.
The twists that occur as the show — which is frequently hilarious — surges to a breathtaking conclusion leave us with disturbing questions about both characters.

To say much more about the plot of the play would be to spoil its major twist, but its author Max Wolf Friedlich threads the strange dance between the two lead characters with a steady build-up of revelation and tension.
'Job' is Oleanna for the digital age, in which the stakes are much higher and the competition among America's superfluous elite is even fiercer.
What passes for a session between a troubled woman and a probing therapist has a valid thematic purpose but can't avoid culminating in an implausible conclusion of the butler did it variety.
